scheme_name: Scheme or assistance for Start Ups/ Innovation: Assistance to Startups having a Significant Impact on Society
description:
The "Assistance to Startups having a Significant Impact on Society" scheme is a pivotal initiative launched by the Government of India to foster innovation and entrepreneurship in the country.

This scheme was officially launched on January 16, 2016, as part of the broader Startup India initiative.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance and support to startups that are working towards creating social impact.

The government aims to encourage startups that address critical social issues such as healthcare, education, agriculture, and environmental sustainability.

The measurable target of this scheme includes the support of at least 10,000 startups over a period of five years.

The scheme is designed to provide financial assistance in the form of grants and equity funding.

Startups can receive funding of up to INR 50 lakhs per project.

This funding is aimed at helping startups develop their products and services that can significantly benefit society.

The assistance is not limited to financial support but also includes mentorship and access to networks.

Eligible startups must be registered as a private limited company, partnership firm, or a limited liability partnership.

The startups must have been incorporated within the last five years to qualify for the scheme.

Moreover, the startups must have a unique product or service that is innovative and has the potential for commercialization.

The annual turnover of the startup should not exceed INR 25 crores in any financial year.

To apply for the scheme, startups must submit an online application through the official Startup India portal.

The application process requires detailed information about the startup's business model, product details, and the social impact it aims to achieve.

Startups must also provide a detailed project report outlining the objectives, methodology, and expected outcomes of their project.

Required documents include the certificate of incorporation, PAN card, and a detailed business plan.

Once the application is submitted, it undergoes a rigorous evaluation process by a committee of experts.

The evaluation process typically takes about 30 to 45 days from the date of application submission.

Successful applicants receive funding in a phased manner based on the achievement of specific milestones.

The disbursement schedule is aligned with the project timelines and milestones set in the project report.

The scheme is implemented by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).

The DPIIT is responsible for overseeing the evaluation process and disbursing funds to eligible startups.

Contact details for the DPIIT can be found on their official website, which provides additional resources and support for startups.

Startups that receive funding under this scheme are also provided with access to various government resources and programs.

These resources include incubation centers, mentorship programs, and networking opportunities with industry experts.

The scheme encourages collaboration between startups and established businesses to foster innovation.

In addition to financial support, the government also provides tax benefits to eligible startups.

Startups registered under this scheme can avail of a three-year tax holiday in the first seven years of their operations.

This tax exemption is applicable to startups with an annual turnover of up to INR 100 crores.

The government also provides a 100% exemption on capital gains tax for investments made in eligible startups.

The scheme has seen significant participation from various sectors, including technology, healthcare, and education.

As of October 2023, over 60,000 startups have registered under the Startup India initiative.

The government has disbursed over INR 1,000 crores in funding to various startups under this scheme.

The success stories of startups funded under this scheme include companies that have developed innovative solutions for waste management, affordable healthcare, and sustainable agriculture.

The government continuously monitors the impact of funded startups on society through various metrics.

These metrics include the number of jobs created, the social issues addressed, and the overall economic impact.

The scheme also encourages startups to focus on sustainable practices and social responsibility.

Startups are encouraged to align their business models with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

The government provides additional support for startups that are led by women and marginalized communities.

Special initiatives are in place to promote inclusivity and diversity within the startup ecosystem.

The scheme is part of a larger strategy to position India as a global hub for innovation and entrepreneurship.

The government aims to create a conducive environment for startups to thrive and contribute to the economy.

The assistance provided under this scheme is expected to create a multiplier effect in the economy by generating employment and fostering innovation.

The scheme is regularly updated to incorporate feedback from stakeholders and adapt to the changing needs of the startup ecosystem.

The government also collaborates with various private sector organizations to enhance the support provided to startups.

This collaboration includes partnerships with venture capital firms and industry associations.

The scheme has received positive feedback from the startup community for its comprehensive support structure.

Overall, the "Assistance to Startups having a Significant Impact on Society" scheme represents a significant commitment by the Government of India to promote entrepreneurship and innovation.

By providing targeted support to startups that address pressing social issues, the government aims to create a more inclusive and sustainable society.

The scheme reflects the government's recognition of the crucial role that startups play in driving economic growth and social change.

Through this initiative, the government is not only investing in individual startups but also in the future of the Indian economy.

This scheme is a vital component of India's broader economic strategy and development goals.
